The film follows awkward college student Casper Galloway, who reluctantly agrees to watch over his grandfather’s mysterious occult shop while his mother attends an award ceremony. Surrounded by oddities and ancient relics, Casper inadvertently unleashes a powerful curse when a mysterious skull-topped urn is broken. The curse is no ordinary one: anyone who makes eye contact with Casper and his group is doomed to take their own life, only to rise again as a bizarre hybrid of zombie and demon—dubbed a “zemon.” As zemons begin to spread at an alarming rate, the once-ordinary day spirals into a chaotic fight for survival. Casper, along with a ragtag group of college friends, must piece together the right ingredients for a reversal ritual before sunrise. With a confined Winnebago as their base of operations, the group frantically scours local haunts—from gas stations to graveyards—evading their monstrous pursuers while battling inner doubts and interpersonal tension. The film cleverly balances outrageous gore with slapstick comedy, meta-horror references, and quirky character dynamics. Veteran actor Christopher Lloyd adds flair as Casper’s eccentric grandfather, offering both exposition and comic relief. The story concludes with a time-reversing ritual that nearly restores normalcy—until the urn is seen teetering again, hinting at another disaster. Bold, bizarre, and unapologetically fun, it’s a cult gem for lover of genre mashups.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: In the 1950s, The Century Series defined an era of aviation during the Cold War, charting a metamorphosis from one era to another. Jets were in their infancy, and many milestones, including the sound barrier, loomed large. In an arms race with the Soviet Union, a rising superpower, the U.S. got to work developing a variety of impressive fighter jets, now known as the Century Series. Starting with the F-100, the first production airplane to break the sound barrier in level flight, we explore how the century series pioneered new airplane designs, including the aerodynamic coke bottle shape made famous by the F-102. The F-104, a missile with a man in it inspired a generation of pilots. The F-105 looked like a fighter but was a bomber in disguise. As a series, their legacy is evident in modern fighter jets.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: For nearly sixty years the Learjet came to define a new class of luxury airplane the business jet. Now, the last Learjet ever is being assembled at the Wichita-based production facility in The Aviation Capital of the World. Speaking with aviation icons past and present, we get an intimate look at a company that shaped aviation as we know it today. From its record-setting performance achievements to its outsized role in popular culture, the Learjets place in history is here to stay, long after the production lines shut down.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Early Space Exploration was defined by a Space race between the United States and the Soviet Union in a quest for national bragging rights. Major milestones like the first artificial Earth satellite, landing on the moon, and eventually creating the International Space Station (ISS) in 1993. Astronauts experience a psychological sensation called The Overview Effect. The ISS marked a new focus on international collaboration in Space. On the ISS, scientists are conducting novel research that is revolutionizing our understanding of life on earth -- from monitoring air pollution to fermenting beer. With the ISS expected to shut down in the coming decades, private space stations may play a larger role in the future of space- and exploration.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: From cave drawings to the identification of star constellations in the night sky, the cosmos has fascinated humankind. Space exploration also provides a unique vantage to look back at Earth. Satellite sensing enables new discoveries about climate change, natural disasters, and civilization. Researchers high in the Rocky Mountains are using satellites, and more than 50 different sensor types to create prediction models of complex watersheds. Mapping technology has become an irreplaceable part of our daily lives and helps plan everything from vaccine distribution, to chimpanzee populations. With the exponential increase in satellites in recent years, comes a need for more space infrastructure, and new challenges like space debris. The opportunities in space exploration are greater than ever but for a burgeoning space economy, so are the challenges.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Technological advances and private investments have enabled a new era in space exploration. Billionaires and private equity are leading the charge, at times in partnership with public space agencies. The impacts are profound in the variety and frequency of space activity. One where anyone can be a citizen astronaut, and for companies a customer. Space for Humanity is working towards a vision where anyone can be an astronaut, and Astro Access took that even further when they crewed a training mission entirely with people with disabilities. Space exploration is more ambitious today than ever before, yet the impact of commercialization with private astronauts, and private space stations - remains to be seen.

programme.title: Behind the Wings

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: From the delivery of packages and medical supplies to the potential of Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft as a form of urban transportation, drone and eVTOL technologies are rapidly changing the future of how we move. In Silicon Valley, a startup is working towards FAA certification on a first-generation flying taxi that could revolutionize how we commute and travel. On a drone test site on the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma, drone companies test new ways to transport medical supplies by drone. In Baltimore a drone delivers the first organ for human transplant. And in Bentonville, Arkansas, DroneUp and Walmart partner to deliver packages by drone to more than six million Americans. It sounds like the future, but it's happening today!

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Explore the design, deployment, and discoveries of the James Webb Space Telescope, one of the most ambitious scientific instruments ever built. Meet the Engineers and scientists who dedicated their careers to designing and building Webb. From the development of new technologies to the intricate process of deploying the telescope in space, Webb is unlike any telescope ever made. Now Webb's data is rolling in, enabling new scientific discoveries about the formation of galaxies and the origins of life. Webb is changing our fundamental understanding of the universe and our place in it.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: Come behind the scenes of one of the most advanced military aircraft in the world. From its 5th generation design to its technological breakthroughs, the F-35 is a formidable machine. At Lockheed Martin's mile-long assembly line in Fort Worth Texas, F-35s are meticulously built. At the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, cadets learn how the F-35 fits into a modern combat environment. And at Miramar Naval Base in San Diego, CA, get an inside look at the training and daily life of the pilots who fly the F-35 operationally.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: A continued exploration of the Artemis missions, building on Episode 404 of Behind the Wings. Look back at Apollo to understand what we learned from going to the moon for the first time. Follow the progress of the program, from the development of new lunar architecture to the training of the astronauts who will take the next steps on the moon. In a Virtual Reality lab at Lockheed Martin Space, Engineers discuss the design of the Orion spacecraft. At Kennedy Space Center, technicians reflect on the learnings from Artemis I. At NASA's Johnson Space Center, astronauts are training for Artemis II, the first Artemis crewed mission. Meet the diverse team working on the program and discover how returning to the Moon is a crucial step towards new scientific discoveries, a cis-lunar economy, and inspiring the next generation of explorers.

programme.title: Behind the Wings
programme.desc: From its incredible history to its unique design features, we're taking an inside look at the Super Guppy! In 1962, President Kennedy made the bold claim to put an American on the moon by the end of the decade. However, the components required for Apollo were massive and assembled nationwide. For Apollo to launch on time, NASA needed an aircraft larger than anything the world had ever seen. Since Apollo, the Super Guppy has completed hundreds of missions for NASA, the DOD, and even worldwide. Five Super Guppies were constructed, and today only one remains flying.

programme.title: Her War, Her Story: World War II
programme.desc: Narrated by actress Jane Lynch, HER WAR, HER STORY: WORLD WAR II tells the story of World War II seen from a new perspective, through the eyes of women who witnessed and served in the war. Focusing on the role of women in history's most violent conflict, the documentary tells the individual stories of more than two dozen women caught up in World War II, from the American home front to Auschwitz concentration camp in Poland. Included in this hour-long film are the personal stories of the incredible women who served in uniform in the military or were Rosie the Riveters at home building the tools of war. First person interviews, archival footage and never before seen photos demonstrate how women were equal to men in patriotism, service and steadfastness in critical moments.
